title: DesignRevisionFidelityAnchor
description: The fidelity anchor: the machine-readable content of the six `design_revision` JSON blob columns, decoded and bundled. ADR 0021 section 2 makes divergence from an approved design revision a defect, which is undecidable while those columns are bare `type: string` with no parseable contract; this document is what an implementation is diffed against. The bundle is one object per `design_revision` row, keyed by each column's name minus its `Json` suffix, so that cross-column rules (a `stateSet.boardId` must resolve into `boardSet`) are checkable in ONE validation rather than six independent ones. TWO anchors exist by operator decision `a1c7d904-3b8e-4f21-9d6e-5c2f81b7a390`: this schema is what the MACHINE diffs against, and Penpot (`penpotFileId`/`penpotPageId`) is what a HUMAN reviewer reads. Where they disagree, the disagreement is itself a finding. NOT EXPRESSIBLE HERE, and deliberately absent rather than forgotten: the seventh rule `designerExecutionId NOT IN reviewExecutionIdsJson`. It compares a field of the record (`designExecutionId` column) against the `reviewExecutionIds` array, so no document constraint can state it; it is a validator assertion, implemented in `DesignRevisionFidelityAnchorValidator`. CANONICAL FORM is a precondition for diffing and is therefore a VALIDATION requirement, not only a formatting one: object keys sorted lexicographically at every level, arrays sorted by the sort key each subschema declares in `x-sort-key`, and no insignificant whitespace. A row that parses but is not canonical is refused, because two encodings of the same revision must be byte-identical to be diffable at all.

boardIds.description: Decoded `boardIdsJson`. A revision asserting no board is a revision that can be diffed against nothing, so `minItems` is 1.

responsiveTargets.description: Decoded `responsiveTargetsJson`. The breakpoint vocabulary is the design-system link.

statesRepresented.description: Decoded `statesRepresentedJson`. Every `boardId` here must resolve into `boardIds`; that cross-column rule is checked by the validator, not by JSON Schema.

artifactRefs.description: Decoded `artifactRefsJson`. `minItems` is 0: a revision may honestly carry no extra artifact.

reviewExecutionIds.description: Decoded `reviewExecutionIdsJson`. `minItems` is 0 because a draft revision has had no reviewer yet; that is a distinct state from claiming reviews happened.

reviewScope.description: Decoded `reviewScopeJson`, or JSON `null` when the nullable column is NULL. Nullable is PRESERVED; what is refused is an object carrying keys this document does not name.

boardId.description: A board id that can be cross-checked against something. A free-text board id cannot be resolved against `boardSet`, which is what makes `stateSet.boardId` checkable.

boardSet.description: Subschema 1 of 6 -- `design_revision.boardIdsJson`. `providerFileId` is REQUIRED inside the blob, which is what closes the nullable-`penpotFileId` hole: it makes the Q5 coherence check enforceable by validation instead of by a separate check nobody runs.

provider.description: Closed vocabulary: a board is only describable through a provider the platform actually integrates.

providerFileId.description: The provider's file identifier for this board. Required, so a revision cannot name a board while leaving the human anchor unopenable.

boardName.description: Optional display name. Constrained rather than free text: an unchecked string here is a claim the platform cannot check.

responsiveSet.description: Subschema 2 of 6 -- `design_revision.responsiveTargetsJson`. The breakpoint vocabulary is THE design-system link: these names must match the product's declared design-system revision, which is what P2 already requires to be named.

breakpoint.description: Closed vocabulary. An open string here would let a revision name a breakpoint no design system declares, and 'did the implementation render the mobile board' would stay an opinion.

minViewportWidthCss.description: Lower bound of the breakpoint in CSS pixels.

stateSet.description: Subschema 3 of 6 -- `design_revision.statesRepresentedJson`. `boardId` here MUST resolve into the same bundle's `boardSet`: a cross-column referential-integrity rule JSON Schema cannot express across two properties, so `DesignRevisionFidelityAnchorValidator` checks it over the bundle. That is what makes 'every named state has a board' checkable, which today it is not.

stateKey.description: The named state. Not an enum: checkpoint 003 does not fix a state vocabulary, and inventing one would be a vocabulary this document has no authority to set.

artifactSet.description: Subschema 4 of 6 -- `design_revision.artifactRefsJson`. `minItems: 0` is honest -- a revision may carry no extra artifact. What the enum buys is that 'artifact' stops meaning whatever the writer meant.

ref.description: The reference itself, in the form its `kind` implies.

executionIdSet.description: Subschema 5 of 6 -- `design_revision.reviewExecutionIdsJson`. Sorted lexicographically, which is the sort key for an array of strings; `x-sort-key` is null because there is no member property to sort by. This is the array the seventh rule reads: the validator asserts `designerExecutionId` is not a member.

reviewScope.description: Subschema 6 of 6 -- `design_revision.reviewScopeJson`, the only nullable one of the six. Nullable is PRESERVED -- JSON `null` validates. What is REFUSED is an object carrying keys this document does not name, which is precisely the `null` / `{}` / arbitrary-keys confusion. The enum stops a reviewer claiming a dimension nobody can check.
